pr_title: fix potential memory leak in PKCS12_add_key_ex()
pr_body:
function must make sure memorry allocated for `p8` gets freed in error path. Issue reported by LuMingYinDetect

Fixes #24453
pr_comments:
Thank you for comments. the new version keeps  call to `PKCS8_PRIV_KEY_INFO_free()`  in error branch. The thing is both functions (`PKCS12_SAFEBAG_create0_p8inf()` and `PKCS12_SAFEBAG_create_pkcs8_encrypt_ex()`) take an ownership of p8 if they are successful.

EDIT: ignore this revision, @slontis is right I was wrong.
now there is a version as proposed by @slontis, I like it.
This pull request is ready to merge

Merged to master, and cherry-picked back to openssl-3.3, openssl-3.2, openssl-3.1 and openssl-3.0.
Thank you for your contribution.

issue_context.title: There is a memory leak vulnerability at line 250 in the /openssl/crypto/pkcs12/p12_crt.c file.
issue_context.body:
At line 244 in the /openssl/crypto/pkcs12/p12_crt.c file, a pointer variable named p8 is defined. At line 247, the EVP_PKEY2PKCS8 function allocates a dynamic memory area for this variable. If the if statement at line 247 returns false, it indicates that the dynamic memory allocation for p8 was successful. When the if statement at line 249 returns true, the program will jump to the err label via a goto statement at line 250. During this process, the dynamic memory area pointed to by p8 is neither freed, as it is in line 254, nor is it freed in the err label, leading to a memory leak vulnerability, as illustrated below (note that the marked paths in the diagram do not match my description; refer to my description for accuracy):
https://github.com/LuMingYinDetect/openssl_defects/blob/main/openssl_25.png

review_comments: Nit: this check is not needed - `..._free()` calls check for `NULL`.
